study_identification_part.si_4_title: Cell type-specific manifestations of cortical thickness heterogeneity in schizophrenia

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Quantile regression was used to establish normative ranges (5%, 50%, 95% percentiles) for cortical thickness as a function of age and sex. The model included linear age, quadratic age, sex, and age-by-sex interaction terms. Bootstrapping was used to estimate confidence intervals.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: Quantile regression was used to obtain a normative range of regional CTh variation as a function of age and sex; For the participant with index i, sexi encodes the participant's sex (male: 0, female: 1), agei is the participant's age. Under this model, β0 is the estimated regional CTh for a male of age A, β1 is the between-sex difference in CTh at age A, β2 is the rate at which CTh changes per year at age A, while β3 and β4 model the sex-by-age interaction and quadratic age effects, respectively.

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Cortical thickness (CTh) measured from T1-weighted MRI using FreeSurfer, averaged over vertices comprising each of 34 cortical regions (left hemisphere) of the Desikan-Killiany atlas. CTh was estimated based on the distance separating the gray and white matter surfaces.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: One of the most frequently reported MRI findings in schizophrenia is reduced cortical thickness (CTh); CTh was estimated for each surface vertex based on the distance separating the gray and white matter surfaces and averaged over all vertices comprising each of the 68 cortical regions (34 per hemisphere) of the Desikan-Killiany atlas.

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: The normative model included four explanatory variables: (1) linear age term, (2) quadratic age term (age squared), (3) sex (binary: male=0, female=1), and (4) sex-by-age interaction term. Additionally, site effects were removed via ComBat harmonization prior to modeling.
